sections.name: Why You Get Goosebumps
lines: Get cold, or hear a song you love, and your skin does this.
Every hair on your body has a tiny muscle attached to its root.
When you're cold, your nerves tell those muscles to squeeze, pulling each hair straight up.
For furry animals, standing hairs trap a thick layer of warm air.
And when they're scared, puffed up fur makes them look bigger. Like a cat.
We lost most of our fur, but we kept the reflex.
So goosebumps are a leftover from when our ancestors were a lot hairier.
